notes.title: PostgreSQL Troubleshooting Runbook
notes.content:
# PostgreSQL Troubleshooting Runbook

Comprehensive guide for PostgreSQL database administration and troubleshooting.

---

## 1. Server Down

### Check Database Status
```bash
ps -ef | grep -i postgres | grep data
ls -a
. .dbname
psql / psql -U dbadmin
```

### Verify Database Uptime
```sql
SELECT date_trunc('second', current_timestamp - pg_postmaster_start_time()) AS db_uptime;
SHOW port;
\! date;
hostname -f;
```

> **Note:** If nothing shows, the database is down.

### Check Logs
```bash
cd $PGDATA/log
ls -a
less <logfilename>  # Choose the last log recorded
```

- Check database activity & connection graphic on PEM
- Take snapshots and inform the apps team

---

## 2. Agent Down

### Check PEM Agent Status
```bash
ps -ef | grep -i pem
systemctl status pemagent
date; hostname -f
```

### Restart PEM Agent
```bash
systemctl start pemagent
```

### Verify Agent is Running
```bash
ps -ef | grep -i pem
systemctl status pemagent
date; hostname -f
```

---

## 3. Total Connections as Percentage of max_connections

### Check Connection Count
```bash
ps -ef | grep -i postgres | grep data
ls -a
. .dbname
psql / psql -U dbadmin
```

```sql
SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity;
SHOW max_connections;
SHOW port;
\! date;
hostname -f;
```

> If active connections > max_connections, check connection graphic on PEM for last 2 days and analyze spike anomalies.

---

## 4. Number of WAL Files

### Check WAL Files
```bash
ps -ef | grep -i postgres | grep data
ls -a
. .dbname
cd $PGDATA/pg_wal
ll | wc -l
psql / psql -U dbadmin
```

```sql
SHOW wal_keep_segments;
SHOW port;
\! date;
hostname -f;
```

> If WAL files exceed capacity, perform housekeeping by deleting older WAL files (keep only current month).

---

## 5. Dead Tuple Percentage

### Check Dead Tuples
```bash
ps -ef | grep -i postgres | grep data
ls -a
. .dbname
psql / psql -U dbadmin
```

### Show Schema & Connect
```sql
SHOW search_path;
\l+
\dn
SET search_path TO myschema;
```

### Query Dead Tuples
```sql
SELECT relname, schemaname, n_live_tup, n_dead_tup, last_vacuum, last_autovacuum
FROM pg_stat_user_tables
ORDER BY n_dead_tup DESC
LIMIT 10;

SELECT schemaname, relname, n_live_tup, n_dead_tup, last_vacuum, last_autovacuum
FROM pg_stat_all_tables
WHERE n_dead_tup >= 200000
ORDER BY n_dead_tup DESC;
```

### Check Autovacuum Settings
```sql
SHOW autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor;
SHOW autovacuum_vacuum_threshold;
SHOW autovacuum_analyze_scale_factor;
SHOW autovacuum_analyze_threshold;
```

### Check Autovacuum Running
```sql
SELECT * FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE query LIKE '%autovacuum%'
AND backend_type = 'autovacuum worker';
```

### Vacuum Commands
- `VACUUM` - Won't change disk space, but new data can be inserted into empty space
- `VACUUM FULL` - Changes disk space, but blocks all operations including SELECT

---

## 6. Number of Ungranted Locks / Query Locking

### Connect to Database
```bash
ps -ef | grep -i postgres | grep data
ls -a
. .dbname
psql / psql -U dbadmin
\l+
\c <database_name>
```

### Check Blocked Queries
```sql
SELECT
    blocked_locks.pid AS blocked_pid,
    blocked_activity.usename AS blocked_user,
    blocking_locks.pid AS blocking_pid,
    blocking_activity.usename AS blocking_user,
    blocked_activity.query AS blocked_statement,
    blocking_activity.query AS current_statement_in_blocking_process,
    blocked_activity.application_name AS blocked_application,
    blocking_activity.application_name AS blocking_application
FROM pg_catalog.pg_locks blocked_locks
JOIN pg_catalog.pg_stat_activity blocked_activity ON blocked_activity.pid = blocked_locks.pid
JOIN pg_catalog.pg_locks blocking_locks
    ON blocking_locks.locktype = blocked_locks.locktype
    AND blocking_locks.DATABASE IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.DATABASE
    AND blocking_locks.relation IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.relation
    AND blocking_locks.page IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.page
    AND blocking_locks.tuple IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.tuple
    AND blocking_locks.virtualxid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.virtualxid
    AND blocking_locks.transactionid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.transactionid
    AND blocking_locks.classid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.classid
    AND blocking_locks.objid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.objid
    AND blocking_locks.objsubid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked_locks.objsubid
    AND blocking_locks.pid != blocked_locks.pid
JOIN pg_catalog.pg_stat_activity blocking_activity ON blocking_activity.pid = blocking_locks.pid
WHERE NOT blocked_locks.GRANTED;
```

### Check Running Queries
```sql
SELECT relation::regclass, * FROM pg_locks WHERE NOT GRANTED;
SELECT * FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE pid = <pid>;
```

### Kill Process
```sql
SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid)
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE usename = '<username>';
```

---

## 7. Replication Lag

### Check if Primary or Replica
```sql
SELECT pg_is_in_recovery();  -- true = replica, false = primary
SELECT * FROM pg_stat_wal_receiver;
```

### On Primary Server
```bash
ps -ef | grep -i postgres | grep data
ls -a
. .dbname
psql / psql -U dbadmin
\x
```

### Check Replication Status
```sql
SELECT client_addr, usename, backend_start, write_lag, flush_lag, replay_lag, state, sync_state
FROM pg_stat_replication;
```

> **Note:** If state = streaming, replication is running.

---

## 8. Disk Consumption Percentage

### Check Disk Usage
```bash
df -kh
cd <largest_used_directory>
du -sh *
```

### Connect to Database
```bash
ps -ef | grep -i postgres | grep data
ls -a
. .dbname
psql / psql -U dbadmin
\c <database_name>
```

---

## 9. Check Table Size / Top Tables

### Connect to Database
```sql
\c <database_name>
```

### Top 10 Tables by Size
```sql
WITH RECURSIVE pg_inherit(inhrelid, inhparent) AS (
    SELECT inhrelid, inhparent FROM pg_inherits
    UNION
    SELECT child.inhrelid, parent.inhparent
    FROM pg_inherit child, pg_inherits parent
    WHERE child.inhparent = parent.inhrelid
),
pg_inherit_short AS (
    SELECT * FROM pg_inherit
    WHERE inhparent NOT IN (SELECT inhrelid FROM pg_inherit)
)
SELECT table_schema, TABLE_NAME, row_estimate,
       pg_size_pretty(total_bytes) AS total,
       pg_size_pretty(index_bytes) AS INDEX,
       pg_size_pretty(toast_bytes) AS toast,
       pg_size_pretty(table_bytes) AS TABLE
FROM (
    SELECT *, total_bytes - index_bytes - COALESCE(toast_bytes, 0) AS table_bytes
    FROM (
        SELECT c.oid, nspname AS table_schema, relname AS TABLE_NAME,
               SUM(c.reltuples) OVER (partition BY parent) AS row_estimate,
               SUM(pg_total_relation_size(c.oid)) OVER (partition BY parent) AS total_bytes,
               SUM(pg_indexes_size(c.oid)) OVER (partition BY parent) AS index_bytes,
               SUM(pg_total_relation_size(reltoastrelid)) OVER (partition BY parent) AS toast_bytes,
               parent
        FROM (
            SELECT pg_class.oid, reltuples, relname, relnamespace, pg_class.reltoastrelid,
                   COALESCE(inhparent, pg_class.oid) parent
            FROM pg_class LEFT JOIN pg_inherit_short ON inhrelid = oid
            WHERE relkind IN ('r', 'p')
        ) c
        LEFT JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace
    ) a
    WHERE oid = parent
) a
ORDER BY table_bytes DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

---

## 10. Slow Log

### Navigate to Logs
```bash
ps -ef | grep -i postgres | grep data
ls -a
. .dbname
cd $PGDATA/log
ls -lrth
```

### Count Slow Queries
```bash
cat pgdb-2022-06-03_*.log | grep -i duration | wc -l
cat pgdb-2022-06-03_*.log | grep -i error | wc -l
```

> Analyze queries taking above 3 seconds (duration). Perform `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on slow queries.

---

## 11. Archive Check & Housekeeping

### Navigate to Archive
```bash
cd /backup_DB_rafmpdb01/backup_PPRAFM/archive
```

### Count Files
```bash
find . -type f -printf '%TY-%Tm-%Td-%TH\n' | sort | uniq -c  # per hour
find . -type f -printf '%TY-%Tm-%Td\n' | sort | uniq -c       # per day
find . -type f -printf '%TY-%Tm\n' | sort | uniq -c           # per month
du -sh .                                                       # active files
```

### Find Files by Time
```bash
find . -name '0000000*' -mmin +1400 | wc -l    # by minutes
find . -name '0000000*' -mtime +2 | wc -l      # by days
find . -newermt "2024-11-06 00:00:00" ! -newermt "2024-11-10 23:59:59" | wc -l
```

### Delete Old Files
```bash
find . -name '0000000*' -mmin +1400 -delete    # by minutes
find . -name '0000000*' -mtime +2 -delete      # by days
find . -newermt "2023-04-15 00:00:00" ! -newermt "2023-04-15 23:59:59" -delete
```

---

## 12. ACL (Access Control List)

### Reload Configuration
```sql
SELECT pg_reload_conf();
```

### Check pg_hba Rules
```sql
SELECT * FROM pg_hba_file_rules WHERE database = '{mlflow}';
SELECT * FROM pg_hba_file_rules WHERE user_name = '{pemuser}';
SELECT * FROM pg_hba_file_rules WHERE address = '10.251.38.112';
SHOW port;
\! date;
hostname -f;
```

### Example pg_hba Entry
```
host    postgres        efmuser         10.38.18.68/32          scram-sha-256
```

notes.title: SOP - Create New Database (EDB/PostgreSQL)
notes.content:
# SOP - Create New Database (EDB/PostgreSQL)

Standard Operating Procedure for creating a new EDB PostgreSQL database with replication setup.

---

## Server Information

### Production Environment - PPDOCMAN

| Role | Hostname | IP Address | Port | Mount Point |
|------|----------|------------|------|-------------|
| **Master** | hpebrn | 10.10.10.10 | 9981 | /data/PPD |
| **Standby** | hpetbs | 10.10.10.10 | 9981 | /data/PPD |

---

## 1. Environment Setup

### Create Environment File (.PPDOCMAN)

```bash
export PATH=/usr/edb/as16/bin:$PATH
export PGHOME=/usr/edb/as16
export PGDATA=/data/PPD/edb/16/DATA
export PGDATABASE=postgres
export PGUSER=dbadmin
export PGPORT=9981
```

### Create Data Directory

```bash
sudo mkdir -p /data/PPD/edb/16/DATA
sudo chown postgres:postgres /data/PPD/edb/16/DATA
```

---

## 2. Initialize Database

### For Master Server

```bash
/usr/edb/as16/bin/initdb -D /data/PPD/edb/16/DATA
```

### For Standby Server (Replication)

```bash
time nohup /usr/edb/as16/bin/pg_basebackup \
    -D /data/PPD/edb/16/DATA \
    -p 9866 \
    -h 10.59.92.14 \
    -U replica \
    -RvP \
    -X stream > /tmp/pg_basebackup_PPDOCMAN_22062024.log &
```

---

## 3. Configuration Files

### log.conf - Logging Configuration

```ini
log_destination = 'stderr'
logging_collector = on
log_directory = 'log'
log_filename = 'pgdb-%Y-%m-%d_%H%M%S.log'
log_rotation_size = 20MB
client_min_messages = notice
log_min_messages = warning
log_min_error_statement = error
log_min_duration_statement = 5000
log_duration = off
log_line_prefix = '%t [%p]: user=%u,db=%d,app=%a,client=%h,sql=%e'
log_lock_waits = on
```

### tune.conf - Performance Tuning

```ini
max_connections = 2000
shared_buffers = 3GB
effective_cache_size = 9GB
maintenance_work_mem = 768MB
checkpoint_completion_target = 0.9
wal_buffers = 16MB
default_statistics_target = 100
random_page_cost = 1.1
effective_io_concurrency = 200
work_mem = 10485kB
min_wal_size = 2GB
max_wal_size = 4GB
autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor = '0'
autovacuum_vacuum_threshold = '200000'
```

### replication.conf - Replication Settings

```ini
port = 9981
wal_level = logical
wal_log_hints = on
archive_mode = always
#archive_command = 'rsync -a %p /data/replication_tbs/mcbc/ppcrox/archived_wals/%f'
max_wal_senders = 10
max_replication_slots = 10
#hot_standby = on
wal_keep_size = 3200
listen_addresses = '*'
password_encryption = scram-sha-256
shared_preload_libraries = '$libdir/pg_stat_statements,$libdir/edb_wait_states,$libdir/query_advisor,$libdir/edb_stat_monitor'
```

### audit_log.conf - EDB Audit Configuration

```ini
edb_audit = 'csv'
edb_audit_directory = 'audit_log'
edb_audit_filename = 'audit-%Y-%m-%d_%H%M%S'
edb_audit_rotation_day = 'every'
edb_audit_rotation_size = 20
edb_audit_connect = 'failed'
edb_audit_disconnect = 'none'
edb_audit_statement = 'ddl'
edb_audit_archiver = 'on'
edb_audit_archiver_compress_size_limit = 20
edb_audit_archiver_compress_time_limit = 0
edb_audit_archiver_expire_size_limit = 40
edb_audit_archiver_expire_time_limit = 0
edb_audit_archiver_expire_command = 'cp %p /data/PPDOCMAN/edb/16/DATA/backup_audit_log/'
```

### Include in postgresql.conf

```ini
include = 'log.conf'
include = 'tune.conf'
include = 'replication.conf'
include = 'audit_log.conf'
```

---

## 4. Start Database

```bash
# Check status
/usr/edb/as16/bin/pg_ctl -D /data/PPDOCMAN/edb/16/DATA status

# Start database
/usr/edb/as16/bin/pg_ctl -D /data/PPDOCMAN/edb/16/DATA start
```

---

## 5. Create System Users

### Admin & Monitoring Users

```sql
-- Database Admin
CREATE USER dbadmin ENCRYPTED PASSWORD '****';
ALTER USER dbadmin WITH SUPERUSER;
ALTER USER postgres NOLOGIN;

-- Monitoring User (Nimmon)
CREATE USER nimmon ENCRYPTED PASSWORD '****';
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE postgres TO nimmon;
GRANT pg_read_all_stats TO nimmon;
GRANT pg_monitor TO nimmon;

-- PEM User
CREATE USER pemuser ENCRYPTED PASSWORD '****' SUPERUSER;

-- Replication User (if replication is needed)
CREATE USER replica ENCRYPTED PASSWORD '******' REPLICATION;
```

---

## 6. Create Application Database & User

### Create Database

```sql
CREATE USER apps ENCRYPTED PASSWORD '******';
CREATE DATABASE docman OWNER apps;
REVOKE CONNECT ON DATABASE docman FROM PUBLIC;
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE docman TO apps;
```

### Create Schema

```sql
\c docman

CREATE SCHEMA docman AUTHORIZATION apps;
REVOKE ALL ON SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA docman TO apps;
GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA docman TO apps;
ALTER USER apps SET search_path TO docman;
```

---

## 7. Create Personal Users

```sql
-- User 1
CREATE USER resaldiput ENCRYPTED PASSWORD '******';
REVOKE CONNECT ON DATABASE docman FROM PUBLIC;
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE docman TO resaldiput;

-- User 2
CREATE USER anisa_n_oktavia_x ENCRYPTED PASSWORD '******';
REVOKE CONNECT ON DATABASE docman FROM PUBLIC;
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE docman TO anisa_n_oktavia_x;
```

---

## 8. Create User Profiles

### Level 1 Profile (Personal Users)

```sql
CREATE PROFILE level1;

-- Assign to users
ALTER USER anisa_n_oktavia_x PROFILE level1;
ALTER USER resaldiput PROFILE level1;

-- Configure profile limits
ALTER PROFILE level1 LIMIT
    FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS 3
    PASSWORD_LOCK_TIME 0.003472
    PASSWORD_LIFE_TIME 60
    PASSWORD_REUSE_TIME UNLIMITED
    PASSWORD_REUSE_MAX 12;
```

### Level 2 Profile (Application Users)

```sql
CREATE PROFILE level2;

-- Assign to app user
ALTER USER apps PROFILE level2;

-- No restrictions for app users
ALTER PROFILE level2 LIMIT
    FAILED_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS UNLIMITED
    PASSWORD_LOCK_TIME UNLIMITED
    PASSWORD_LIFE_TIME UNLIMITED
    PASSWORD_REUSE_TIME UNLIMITED
    PASSWORD_REUSE_MAX UNLIMITED;
```

### Verify User Profiles

```sql
SELECT rolname, rolprofile FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'anisa_n_oktavia_x';
SELECT rolname, rolprofile FROM pg_roles WHERE rolprofile = 'level1';
SELECT * FROM DBA_PROFILES WHERE profile = 'LEVEL1';
```

---

## 9. Install Extensions

```sql
SET search_path TO docman;

CREATE EXTENSION edb_wait_states;
CREATE EXTENSION query_advisor WITH SCHEMA docman;
CREATE EXTENSION edb_stat_monitor WITH SCHEMA docman;
CREATE EXTENSION pg_stat_statements;

-- Grant privileges to PEM user
GRANT pg_monitor TO pemuser;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION edb_wait_states_sessions TO pemuser;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION edb_wait_states_data TO pemuser;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION edb_wait_states_queries TO pemuser;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION edb_wait_states_samples TO pemuser;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION edb_wait_states_purge TO pemuser;
```

---

## 10. Configure pg_hba.conf (ACL)

### Add Entries

```
# Replication
host    replication     replica         10.59.213.7/32          trust

# PEM Monitoring
host    all             pemuser         10.251.38.36/32         scram-sha-256

# Application Access
host    docman          apps            10.52.75.75/32          scram-sha-256
```

### Verify ACL Rules

```sql
SELECT * FROM pg_hba_file_rules WHERE user_name = '{apps}';
SHOW port;
\! date;
hostname -f;
```

---

## 11. Create EDB Resource Manager (ERM)

### Create Resource Group

```sql
-- Connect to database first

-- Create resource group
CREATE RESOURCE GROUP resource_1;
SELECT * FROM edb_resource_group;

-- Set CPU limit to 50%
ALTER RESOURCE GROUP resource_1 SET cpu_rate_limit TO 50;

-- Assign user to resource group
ALTER USER apps SET edb_resource_group TO resource_1;

-- Verify
SELECT * FROM edb_all_resource_groups;
\drds
```

---

## Quick Reference Commands

| Action | Command |
|--------|--------|
| Check status | `pg_ctl -D $PGDATA status` |
| Start DB | `pg_ctl -D $PGDATA start` |
| Stop DB | `pg_ctl -D $PGDATA stop` |
| Reload config | `pg_ctl -D $PGDATA reload` |
| Connect | `psql -U dbadmin -d postgres` |
